paragraphs: Cheshire has two councils that look after children in care: Cheshire East Council and Cheshire West and Chester Council. Each runs its own fostering service, and the independent agencies shown above also place children across the county. Our separate Cheshire East and Cheshire West and Chester pages cover each council area in more detail.

Cheshire West and Chester recruits with Halton and Warrington through Foster4, a shared council fostering service. In 2022 Foster4 said more than 450 households fostered with it across Cheshire, and it launched support packages for its carers that included the use of a seven-seater pool car, swimming passes, equipment and local out-of-hours help. In 2023 the council also sought specialist carers, ideally with experience of working with children, to give family homes to children in long-term care who have been through difficult early experiences, with a professional fee that it put at £52,000 a year plus allowances.

Cheshire East said in December 2023 that it was caring for more than 540 children and young people, and that a shortage of local foster homes meant some lived outside the borough. That month both Cheshire councils joined six neighbouring councils in Cheshire and Merseyside in sharing more than £2.3 million from the Department for Education to create a larger regional recruitment hub and to expand the Mockingbird programme, in which a hub carer supports a group of six to ten fostering families.
Pay and support differ between the two councils and the agencies above, so it is worth talking to two or three of them and asking about fees, training and local support groups before you apply.
